title: Isaiah Chapter 25 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 25 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 25 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 25.

questions.question: What does the speaker intend to do to the LORD in Isaiah 25:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Exalt Him
questions.explanation: The speaker states, 'I will exalt thee' (Isaiah 25:1), indicating the intention to elevate and honor the LORD.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 25:2, what has the LORD made of a defenced city?
questions.correctAnswer: A ruin
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'thou hast made of a defenced city a ruin' (Isaiah 25:2).

questions.question: What will the strong people do according to Isaiah 25:3?
questions.correctAnswer: Glorify the LORD
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'Therefore shall the strong people glorify thee' (Isaiah 25:3).

questions.question: In Isaiah 25:4, to whom has the LORD been a strength?
questions.correctAnswer: The poor
questions.explanation: The verse indicates, 'For thou hast been a strength to the poor' (Isaiah 25:4).

questions.question: True or False: In Isaiah 25:1, the speaker acknowledges the wonderful things done by the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The speaker praises the LORD for 'thou hast done wonderful things' (Isaiah 25:1).

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 25:2 states that a palace of strangers will be built.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'a palace of strangers to be no city; it shall never be built' (Isaiah 25:2).

questions.question: According to Isaiah 25:5, what will the LORD do to the noise of strangers?
questions.correctAnswer: Bring it down
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Thou shalt bring down the noise of strangers' (Isaiah 25:5).

questions.question: What type of feast will the LORD make in Isaiah 25:6?
questions.correctAnswer: A feast of fat things
questions.explanation: The verse describes 'a feast of fat things' (Isaiah 25:6).

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 25:8 says that the LORD will wipe away tears from off all faces.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces' (Isaiah 25:8).

questions.question: In Isaiah 25:10, what will happen to Moab according to the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: It will be trodden down
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that 'Moab shall be trodden down under him' (Isaiah 25:10).

questions.question: What will the LORD destroy in Isaiah 25:7?
questions.correctAnswer: The covering over all people
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'he will destroy in this mountain the face of the covering cast over all people' (Isaiah 25:7).

questions.question: True or False: The fortress of the high fort will remain safe according to Isaiah 25:12.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'the fortress of the high fort of thy walls shall he bring down' (Isaiah 25:12).

questions.question: What comes first in Isaiah 25:1-4?
options: The statement of the LORD's faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: The statement of the LORD's faithfulness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:1 begins with the speaker exalting the LORD for His wonderful acts and faithfulness.

questions.question: What will happen when the LORD wipes away the tears from all faces in Isaiah 25:8?
questions.correctAnswer: There will be joy
questions.explanation: The context of the verse suggests that wiping away tears signifies comfort and joy, especially as it follows the statement of victory over death.

questions.question: What will the LORD do with the pride of the nations in Isaiah 25:11?
questions.correctAnswer: Bring it down
questions.explanation: The verse states that He 'shall bring down their pride' (Isaiah 25:11).

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 25 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 25 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 25:5, what will happen to the noise of strangers?
options: It shall be as the heat in a dry place, brought low
It shall be increased like a storm
It shall be ignored and forgotten
It shall be celebrated among the people
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be as the heat in a dry place, brought low
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:5 states that the noise of strangers will be brought down as heat in a dry place, meaning it will be subdued and diminished. This connects with the idea in Isaiah 25:4 of God being a refuge from storms, showing His power over chaos and distress.

questions.question: What kind of feast does the LORD of hosts prepare on this mountain according to Isaiah 25:6?
options: A feast of fat things full of marrow and wines well refined
A simple meal of bread and water
A feast of bitter herbs and salt
A feast only for the priests
questions.correctAnswer: A feast of fat things full of marrow and wines well refined
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:6 describes a lavish feast prepared by the LORD of hosts for all people, symbolizing abundance and blessing. This feast contrasts with the destruction mentioned in earlier verses, emphasizing God's provision and salvation.

questions.question: What will God destroy on this mountain as described in Isaiah 25:7?
options: The face of the covering and the vail over all nations
questions.correctAnswer: The face of the covering and the vail over all nations
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:7 speaks of God removing the spiritual covering and veil that blinds all people and nations, indicating a revelation of truth and end of ignorance. This complements the joyous feast of Isaiah 25:6, showing God's saving power.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 25:8 describe God's victory over death?
options: He will swallow up death in victory and wipe away tears from all faces
He will allow death to reign forever
He will make death a friend to believers
He will ignore death and focus on life only
questions.correctAnswer: He will swallow up death in victory and wipe away tears from all faces
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:8 declares that God will conquer death completely and comfort all people by wiping away their tears. This assurance of triumph over death is central to Christian hope and ties to the deliverance promised in verses 6 and 7.

questions.question: What lesson about trust in God can we learn from Isaiah 25:9's declaration?
options: That waiting on the LORD leads to salvation and rejoicing
That God only saves instantly without waiting
That salvation is earned by human effort
That God is distant and unresponsive
questions.correctAnswer: That waiting on the LORD leads to salvation and rejoicing
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:9 highlights the blessing of patiently waiting for God, who ultimately saves and brings joy. This complements the promises of deliverance and comfort in verses 7 and 8, encouraging faith and perseverance.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 25:10 states that Moab will be exalted and protected by the hand of the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:10 actually says that Moab shall be trodden down under the hand of the LORD, like straw on a dunghill, indicating judgment rather than exaltation. This contrasts with the protection promised to the needy in earlier verses like Isaiah 25:4.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 25:4, how does God serve those in distress?
options: As a strength, refuge, and shadow from heat and storms
As a strict lawgiver without mercy
questions.correctAnswer: As a strength, refuge, and shadow from heat and storms
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:4 describes God as a source of strength and protection for the poor and needy in distress, providing shelter and relief. This theme of God's care is foundational to the comforting promises in the middle verses of the chapter.

questions.question: What practical Christian virtue is taught by the promise in Isaiah 25:8 that God will wipe away tears from all faces?
options: Hope in God's ultimate comfort and victory over suffering
Ignoring pain and pretending all is well
questions.correctAnswer: Hope in God's ultimate comfort and victory over suffering
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:8 encourages believers to trust in God's promise to end suffering and sorrow, fostering hope and patience. This connects with the joyful salvation in verse 9 and God's protective strength in verse 4.

questions.question: How does the imagery in Isaiah 25:5 of the 'branch of the terrible ones' being brought low relate to the overall message of the chapter?
options: It symbolizes God's triumph over prideful enemies, reinforcing His strength for the needy
It encourages joining the terrible ones
It predicts the rise of terrible nations
It describes a natural disaster unrelated to God
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes God's triumph over prideful enemies, reinforcing His strength for the needy
questions.explanation: The 'branch of the terrible ones' in Isaiah 25:5 represents oppressive powers brought low by God, which aligns with His role as protector and refuge in Isaiah 25:4 and the promise of salvation in verses 7 and 8.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 25:7 promise will happen if God destroys the 'face of the covering' and 'vail' over all nations?
options: People will see the truth and receive salvation
People will remain blind to God's works
Nations will be overwhelmed by darkness
Only one nation will be saved
questions.correctAnswer: People will see the truth and receive salvation
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:7 refers to God removing spiritual blindness, which allows people to perceive divine truth, linking to the feast of salvation in verse 6 and the wiping away of tears in verse 8.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 25:12 describes God strengthening the fortress walls of the city.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:12 says that God will bring down the fortress of the high fort of the walls to the dust, indicating judgment and destruction rather than strengthening. This follows the theme of humbling the proud in the chapter.

questions.question: How can Isaiah 25:6-8 encourage a believer struggling with grief and despair?
options: By assuring them of God's provision, victory over death, and wiping away of tears
By telling them to hide their feelings permanently
By urging them to rely solely on human wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: By assuring them of God's provision, victory over death, and wiping away of tears
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:6-8 offers hope through God's feast of blessing, His destruction of spiritual blindness, and His swallowing up of death, providing comfort to those in sorrow. This encourages trust and perseverance in faith.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 25:11 imply about God's attitude toward pride and spoils of the proud?
options: God will bring down their pride along with their spoils
God will build pride up as a virtue
questions.correctAnswer: God will bring down their pride along with their spoils
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:11 illustrates how God actively humbles the proud by stripping away their gains, consistent with the judgment themes in verses 10 and 12, and His protection over the humble in verse 4.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 25:3 teaches that the strong and terrible nations will glorify and fear the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:3 states that strong peoples and terrible nations will glorify and fear God, showing that all will ultimately acknowledge His power, which is consistent with the chapter's theme of God's sovereignty.

questions.question: What comfort does Isaiah 25:4 offer to those facing distress and oppression?
options: God is a refuge and shadow protecting them from storms and heat
They must rely on their own strength alone
They should seek revenge on their oppressors
questions.correctAnswer: God is a refuge and shadow protecting them from storms and heat
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:4 provides assurance that God is a source of strength and protection for the poor and needy, reinforcing the practical Christian virtue of trusting God in hardship as seen throughout the chapter.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 25 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 25.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 25:9, what is the response of the people on that day regarding God?
options: Lo, this is our God; we have waited for him, and he will save us
Behold, we are lost without him
questions.correctAnswer: Lo, this is our God; we have waited for him, and he will save us
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:9 states that on that day it shall be said, 'Lo, this is our God; we have waited for him, and he will save us,' expressing the people's gladness and rejoicing in salvation.

questions.question: What imagery is used in Isaiah 25:10 to describe how Moab will be defeated?
options: Trodden down under him, even as straw is trodden down for the dunghill
Swept away like dust in the wind
questions.correctAnswer: Trodden down under him, even as straw is trodden down for the dunghill
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:10 uses the simile of straw being trodden down for the dunghill to illustrate how Moab will be trampled under the hand of the LORD.

questions.question: In Isaiah 25:11, the LORD is compared to someone spreading forth his hands in the midst of them. What action is this compared to?
options: As he that swimmeth spreadeth forth his hands to swim
As a warrior wielding a sword
As a builder raising a wall
questions.correctAnswer: As he that swimmeth spreadeth forth his hands to swim
questions.explanation: Verse 11 uses the simile of a swimmer spreading his hands to swim to describe the LORD spreading forth His hands to bring down the pride of His enemies.

questions.question: What will happen to the fortress and high walls according to Isaiah 25:12?
options: He shall bring them down, lay low, and bring to the ground, even to the dust
They will be repaired and fortified
They will be hidden by a covering
questions.correctAnswer: He shall bring them down, lay low, and bring to the ground, even to the dust
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:12 declares that the fortress and high walls will be destroyed and brought down to dust, symbolizing complete defeat.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage resonates with Isaiah 25:8’s theme of God swallowing up death in victory?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 49:15
questions.explanation: Psalm 49:15 speaks of God redeeming the soul from the power of the grave, paralleling Isaiah 25:8’s theme of God swallowing up death in victory.

questions.question: What feast does the LORD prepare for all people on the mountain according to Isaiah 25:6?
options: A feast of fat things, a feast of wines on the lees, full of marrow
A feast of bread and water
questions.correctAnswer: A feast of fat things, a feast of wines on the lees, full of marrow
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:6 describes a rich feast prepared by the LORD with fat things full of marrow and refined wines, symbolizing abundant blessing.

questions.question: Isaiah 25:7 speaks of God destroying a 'covering' and a 'vail' over all nations. What do these symbolize?
questions.correctAnswer: Ignorance and blindness
questions.explanation: The 'covering' and 'vail' in Isaiah 25:7 symbolize spiritual ignorance and blindness that God will remove from all peoples.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes Isaiah 25:8’s promise that the LORD will wipe away tears from off all faces?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 21:4
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:4 echoes Isaiah 25:8 by promising that God will wipe away all tears, and there will be no more death or sorrow.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 25:9 indicates that the people’s waiting for God results in gladness and rejoicing in His salvation.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:9 explicitly states the people will be glad and rejoice in salvation after waiting for the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 25:10 refers to the destruction of Jerusalem by the hand of the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:10 specifically mentions Moab being trodden down, not Jerusalem; therefore, the statement is false.

questions.question: What Hebrew word is translated as 'vail' in Isaiah 25:7, and what is its significance?
options: Masah – meaning a covering or blindness
questions.correctAnswer: Masah – meaning a covering or blindness
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Masah' translated as 'vail' in Isaiah 25:7 signifies a covering that causes spiritual blindness, which God promises to remove.

questions.question: How does the author use parallelism in Isaiah 25:8 to emphasize God’s victory over death?
options: By pairing 'swallow up death' with 'wipe away tears' and 'take away rebuke'
By repeating the word 'victory' three times
By using a metaphor of a lion
questions.correctAnswer: By pairing 'swallow up death' with 'wipe away tears' and 'take away rebuke'
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:8 uses parallelism by listing actions of God—swallowing death, wiping tears, removing rebuke—to highlight comprehensive victory and restoration.

questions.question: Which Old Testament event provides a historical context for the destruction imagery used in Isaiah 25:2 about a city made a heap and a palace of strangers?
options: The destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah
The siege of Jerusalem by Assyria
questions.correctAnswer: The destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:2’s imagery of a destroyed city and palace of strangers recalls the devastation of Sodom and Gomorrah, symbolizing total ruin.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 25:4 describe God’s protection of the poor and needy?
options: A strength, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat
A king who rules with power
A judge who punishes the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: A strength, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:4 portrays God as a strength and refuge for the poor in distress, providing comfort like shade from heat.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage is thematically connected to Isaiah 25:6’s feast imagery, symbolizing the messianic banquet?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 19:9
questions.explanation: Revelation 19:9 speaks of the marriage supper of the Lamb, echoing Isaiah 25:6’s imagery of the LORD preparing a rich feast for all people.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 25 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 25 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily revealed in Isaiah 25:1 when the psalmist praises God for His "counsels of old" being "faithfulness and truth"?
questions.correctAnswer: God's immutability
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:1 speaks of God's ancient counsels as characterized by faithfulness and truth, emphasizing that God's plans are unchanging and reliable throughout time, which is the attribute of immutability.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 25:2, what fate does God decree for a city previously fortified and inhabited by strangers?
options: It shall be destroyed and never rebuilt
It shall be purified and made holy
It shall be given to the rightful heirs
It shall be preserved as a memorial
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be destroyed and never rebuilt
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:2 declares that God has made a city a heap and a ruin, specifically a palace of strangers to be no city, and it shall never be built again, indicating destruction and permanent desolation.

questions.question: What theological truth about God’s relationship to the oppressed is taught in Isaiah 25:4?
options: God is a refuge and strength for the poor and needy in distress
God punishes the poor for their sins
God ignores the pleas of the needy in suffering
God favors the rich and powerful over the weak
questions.correctAnswer: God is a refuge and strength for the poor and needy in distress
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:4 reveals that God acts as a strength and refuge to the poor and needy, providing protection and relief in their times of trouble, highlighting His compassion and care for the marginalized.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 25:5 metaphorically describe God's action against the 'noise of strangers' and the 'branch of the terrible ones'?
options: As heat in a dry place being calmed by the shadow of a cloud
As a flood drowning the wicked
As a sword striking down enemies
questions.correctAnswer: As heat in a dry place being calmed by the shadow of a cloud
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:5 uses the metaphor of heat in a dry place being mitigated by the shadow of a cloud to describe God's action in silencing the noise of the strangers and humbling the pride of the terrible ones, showing His power to bring relief and judgment.

questions.question: What eschatological hope is symbolized by the 'feast of fat things' and 'wines on the lees well refined' in Isaiah 25:6?
options: The future messianic banquet where all people are invited
The harvest festival of the Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: The future messianic banquet where all people are invited
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:6 speaks of a sumptuous feast prepared by the LORD on a mountain for all people, symbolizing the messianic banquet representing salvation, fellowship, and God's ultimate provision for His redeemed.

questions.question: Which doctrinal truth about death and resurrection does Isaiah 25:8 communicate?
options: God will swallow up death in victory and wipe away all tears
Only the righteous will escape death
Death is a natural cycle with no divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: God will swallow up death in victory and wipe away all tears
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:8 proclaims that the LORD will decisively conquer death and remove sorrow and reproach from His people, expressing the doctrine of God's ultimate victory over death and the hope of resurrection.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching about salvation and waiting on God is found in Isaiah 25:1 and Isaiah 25:9?
options: God's faithfulness in ancient plans assures believers' joyful salvation after patient waiting
Salvation is immediate and needs no waiting
God's plans are unknown and salvation is uncertain
Waiting on God leads to despair and doubt
questions.correctAnswer: God's faithfulness in ancient plans assures believers' joyful salvation after patient waiting
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:1 praises God's unchanging faithfulness, while Isaiah 25:9 emphasizes rejoicing in salvation after waiting for God, together teaching that God's eternal plans guarantee the joyful salvation of those who patiently trust Him.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 25:10 depict God's judgment on Moab, and what does this signify theologically?
options: Moab will be trampled like straw, symbolizing God's sovereign judgment over nations
Moab will be exalted above other nations
Moab will be spared due to righteousness
Moab will be given special blessings
questions.correctAnswer: Moab will be trampled like straw, symbolizing God's sovereign judgment over nations
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:10 uses the image of Moab being trodden down like straw for the dunghill, illustrating God's sovereign authority to judge and humble proud nations opposing His will.

questions.question: What theological insight about divine humility and human pride is conveyed by the imagery in Isaiah 25:11?
options: God humbles the proud by spreading His hands like a swimmer and bringing down their pride
God elevates the prideful to lead nations
Pride is a virtue rewarded by God
God ignores human pride and lets it flourish
questions.correctAnswer: God humbles the proud by spreading His hands like a swimmer and bringing down their pride
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:11 portrays God’s active humiliation of the proud, using the metaphor of spreading hands like a swimmer, symbolizing deliberate divine action to overthrow human pride and arrogance.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 25:12, what does God's destruction of the fortress and high walls symbolize in a broader redemptive narrative?
options: God breaks down human defenses against Him to establish His kingdom
God preserves earthly kingdoms for all time
Walls and fortresses protect people from God
questions.correctAnswer: God breaks down human defenses against Him to establish His kingdom
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:12's depiction of God bringing down fortresses symbolizes the breaking of human resistance and pride, clearing the way for God's redemptive reign, aligning with the biblical theme of God's triumph over worldly power.

questions.question: What apologetic response does Isaiah 25:7-8 provide to skeptics who claim that death and sorrow are final and irreversible?
options: God will remove the covering over all people, swallow up death in victory, and wipe away all tears
Death and sorrow are permanent and have no divine remedy
Only some people can escape death and sorrow
Skeptics are right; there is no hope beyond death
questions.correctAnswer: God will remove the covering over all people, swallow up death in victory, and wipe away all tears
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:7-8 declares that God will abolish the veil over nations, conquer death, and comfort all people by wiping away tears, countering skeptical claims by affirming God’s sovereign power over death and sorrow, supported also by 1 Corinthians 15:54-55.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God's providential judgment and mercy can be synthesized from Isaiah 25:3 and Isaiah 25:4?
options: God is feared by the strong and terrible nations but is a refuge and strength for the poor and needy
God is only a judge without mercy
God ignores the plight of the poor and needy
God favors the terrible nations over the weak
questions.correctAnswer: God is feared by the strong and terrible nations but is a refuge and strength for the poor and needy
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:3 shows that strong and terrible nations fear God, while Isaiah 25:4 reveals God as refuge and strength for the poor, teaching that God's providence includes just judgment on the proud and merciful care for the humble.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 25:6-7 together typologically prefigure Christ and the ultimate salvation He brings?
options: The LORD’s feast and the removal of the covering point to Christ’s messianic banquet and the lifting of spiritual blindness
They describe only a physical celebration with no spiritual meaning
They focus on Old Testament temple rituals unrelated to Christ
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD’s feast and the removal of the covering point to Christ’s messianic banquet and the lifting of spiritual blindness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:6 depicts a feast for all peoples, and verse 7 speaks of removing the veil over nations, together foreshadowing Christ's messianic banquet (Luke 22:16) and His work in removing spiritual blindness (2 Corinthians 3:14).

questions.question: What overarching narrative arc about God's kingdom and human rebellion is revealed by combining Isaiah 25:2 and Isaiah 25:12?
options: God brings down fortified cities and proud walls, showing His ultimate victory over human rebellion against His kingdom
God supports human kingdoms to remain forever
Human rebellion will never be defeated
God remains passive in the face of human pride
questions.correctAnswer: God brings down fortified cities and proud walls, showing His ultimate victory over human rebellion against His kingdom
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:2 describes the destruction of a fortified city, and Isaiah 25:12 speaks of bringing down high fortresses, together illustrating God's sovereign judgment and triumph over human rebellion, fitting the biblical theme of God's kingdom overcoming worldly powers.

questions.question: What attribute of God is most clearly emphasized in Isaiah 25:9 where the people proclaim, 'This is our God; we have waited for him, and he will save us'?
options: God’s faithfulness to save His people
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness to save His people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 25:9 highlights God’s saving faithfulness as the people joyfully acknowledge that God has fulfilled His promise to save those who waited for Him.
